newsitem.title: USA: Tennant adopts new holder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Tennant adopts new holder rights plan.

text.p: Tennant Co said Tuesday its board adopted a shareholder rights plan that is similiar to the plan that expires on December 23.
Tennant, which makes non-residential floor maintenance equipment, floor coatings and related products, said the new plan was not adopted in response to any current effort to acquire the company.
The new plan grants to Tennant shareholders a preferred share purchase right, which becomes exercisable only if a third party accumulates 20 percent or more of the company's common shares.
In the case of a takeover attempt, the rights allow the holders -- accept the acquiring investor -- to purchase $200 of Tennant common stock for $100, subject to adjustment.

If the company is acquired, each right that has not become void could be exercised for common stock of the acquiring company, or its affiliate, having a market value of twice the right's exercise price, Tennant said.

In certain circumstances, the company may redeem the rights for $.01 each, exchange them for common shares, delay or temporarily suspend the exercisability of the rights, or reduce the 20 percent stock ownership threshold to not less than 10 percent.
Tennant now has about 9,953,000 shares of common stock currently outstanding.

Tennant also said its directors adopted a dividend reinvestment plan that will be available beginning with the December 31 payment. The plan gives current shareholders the opportunity to invest quarterly cash dividends in additional shares of Tennant without incurring any brokerage charges or service fees.
